source.display_title: 05/29/2026 - Vibhor Mishra x Ben Byrne  — Follow Up

setter.evidence: Prospect references being messaged by 'Sophia' and asks whether she is human: 'is this a real person or a chatbot, like, who I've been iMessaging with?'

prospect.name: Vibhor Mishra
prospect.occupation: Software engineer at a startup in New York City
prospect.family_status: Married, has a husband, no children
prospect.training_background: Trained consistently 5 days a week for about 18 months pre-COVID on a friend's bodybuilding split and reached his best shape; fell off after COVID and remote work. Currently aiming for 3 gym days a week, hikes regularly, has done Trevor's free kettlebell workouts about 3 days a week for 3 weeks.
prospect.medical: No conditions disclosed. Reports occasional neck stiffness and intermittent shoulder 'quirks' attributed to sitting about seven hours a day at a desk.

signals: Explicitly benchmarks himself against a former self: rated his physique 8.5 pre-COVID versus 5-6 now
'after COVID hit, and then got off this gym schedule, more work, remote, not much access to the gym, so that's been, I would say, been more of downhill since then'
Confidence loss is the stated driver - wants to take his shirt off at the beach again
Secondary skeptical_bargain_hunter traits appear late: compares the offer to a local in-person personal trainer

goals.text: Build visible upper-body muscle - arms, chest, back - toned rather than bulky
Get back to the physique and confidence he had before COVID, around 8.5 out of 10
Feel confident enough to take his shirt off at the beach and on summer trips
Achieve results in 45 minutes or less per session instead of 90-minute gym sessions, so training fits around work and social life
Train consistently in a way that is sustainable long term rather than an extreme push
A leaner midsection - a 'shredded core' but not a six pack

pains.text: Cannot get to the gym three days a week reliably because of unpredictable late work calls
Has been assembling bits and pieces from different Instagram and YouTube coaches and none of it is working
No structured, progressive plan to follow - named this as the main reason for lack of results
Struggles to hit protein targets as a vegetarian, reaching only 60-70 grams a day
The 90-minute, five-day-a-week routine that previously worked is unsustainable in his current life
Lost motivation because the gym work he was doing produced no results
Lower self-esteem about his body, sharpened by living somewhere he perceives people as very fit
Occasional neck stiffness and shoulder discomfort from about seven hours a day seated

objections.raw_quote: as of now, what I can say is like, it definitely sounds very reasonable and aligned to what I'm looking for. Um, I can give, yeah, I'll give it more thought. If there's any material that you can share to give me more insight about the plan, like in some way or the other, that would help. But again, yeah, I'll give good thought to it and then get back to you with the decision, yeah.
objections.rep_response: Asked an isolating question - 'is it just, I guess, wanting to see the plan and what it might look like that is coming up for you? Or is there anything else?' - then explained that plans are only built after the intake form, and offered an improvised deposit. Did not run the scripted OA moves and let the call end on a text-me-later.

objections.raw_quote: Well, the cost of plan is, I think it's a little on the higher side that I've heard, but I think it's, I would say it's sort of manageable, but it's all have to just evaluate that piece as well.
objections.rep_response: Asked a clarifying question - 'are you saying like, whether it's worth it or if you, if you... I the money to do it' - but never ran the financial picture questions and did not isolate finances as the only blocker before conceding.

objections.raw_quote: if I do, like, a trainer in the gym next to me, like, with a personal trainer, like, just want to evaluate, like, how much does that in person, if it's costing around the same, maybe, like, if I should give. I just want to evaluate those pieces as well, along with this.
objections.rep_response: Pointed out the contradiction with the prospect's stated goal - 'that's kind of like the opposite of what you said you wanted, which is just... doing the same thing, being in the gyms' - then withdrew: 'obviously it's up to you. I'm not here to force you to do anything, but if you want to try to find a personal trainer, I mean, by all means.'

objections.raw_quote: Because I do travel to my home country for a month. So I just want to make sure I don't have anything coming up in the next six months. Otherwise, I'll have to take a break or something for a month
objections.rep_response: Offered to pause and extend: 'worst case, we could just, you know, add on an extra month so that you're not really missing anything while you're traveling.' The prospect rejected the workaround, saying he wants an unbroken six months.

objections.raw_quote: I don't know if you have a kind of a sample plan that you have for, like, a dummy plan that you can just share how it would look like over the six months just to help me get an idea of what I'll be looking to.
objections.rep_response: Half-offered then talked himself out of it - 'I could send over other plans that we've created for other people, but, you know, again, it would just be kind of generic' - and used a tax-planner analogy: 'generally, you join and then they give you the plan.' Proposed label: proof_of_deliverable_before_purchase.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Improvised on the call: 'instead of you just paying a 6K or 9K if you want to do for a year, like, we could put down, like, say, half or 2,000 or something. And that's just to get you started... we can just figure out a payment plan over the next six months for the rest.' No instalment count, schedule or total was stated.

evidence: Prospect committed only to deciding later: 'I'll give good thought to it and then get back to you with the decision'
Ended with 'I'll just evaluate and I'll message you back with, yeah, if I'm like, kind of like joining me from next week or whatsoever'
No payment was collected and no payment link was sent - only a text message exchanging phone numbers
Counter-evidence for a warmer read: prospect said the offer 'definitely sounds very reasonable and aligned to what I'm looking for' and called the price 'sort of manageable'
Counter-evidence for a colder read: he left to compare against a local in-person personal trainer and wanted to check his travel schedule, neither of which was resolved
outcome.next_step: Prospect to text Ben over the weekend or early the following week with a decision. No scheduled follow-up call and no material was agreed to be sent.

notable.note: Two things a manager should see. First, the prospect directly asked whether the person who had been iMessaging him ('Sophia') was a real person or a chatbot, and the rep answered only 'Did you say it was Sophia?' - the question was never answered. Second, the rep skipped the Consequence Frame entirely and never took a commitment check before presenting, then improvised a '$2,000 or half' deposit the moment hesitation appeared, which is a discount-shaped move made from a position of no commitment.

quality.notes: Short turns are frequently attributed to the wrong speaker. Clear inversions include the age exchange at 00:27:28, where 'How old are you right now?' and the answer 'Oh, I'm 35' are both attributed across the two labels incorrectly - content shows the rep asked and the prospect is 35. Also at 00:21:06 and 00:38:01 backchannels are misassigned. Long passages are reliable; role assignment was read from content throughout.
